neighbours.label: the 'of' in a role analogy that names something as 'the X of Y', borrowing a famous person, place or brand as the role (the Mozart of football, the Venice of the north, the Uber of dog walking); 'of' in literal roles, titles, owners and parts stays low
fire: Critics call him the Picasso of pastry chefs.
The startup wants to be the Uber of dog walking.
Locals call the town the Venice of the north.
She was hailed as the Meryl Streep of her generation.
Durian is the Marmite of fruits.
That airport is the DMV of air travel.
He has become the LeBron James of chess.
Austin wants to be the Silicon Valley of the south.
quiet: Critics call him the owner of three pastry shops.
The startup wants to be the maker of a dog walking app.
Locals call the town the capital of the north.
She was hailed as the daughter of a famous actress.
Durian is the national fruit of Malaysia.
That airport is the busiest hub of air travel.
He has become the coach of the chess club.
Austin wants to be the capital of the south.

notes: Found by an analogy concept screen (discovery only): 11/12 role-analogy pairs ('Nashville is the Detroit of country music' vs a plain relation), peaking on 'of'.
